## Introduction

We will store two versions of `HealthWellbeing` in a local *pins*
board. The first contains all 29 studies. The second contains the 18
general-population studies, so we can explore how that restriction
changes the analysis. Both use the variable definitions from the data
dictionary, and both trace back to the same raw file.
[Dataset documentation](04_data_documentation.qmd)

Work from the project root with *box*, *pins*, and the raw file from
the preparation lesson. Runs reuse versions with the same data and
provenance. The instructor can provide a prepared board and its
selection files if you need to catch up.
[Prepare the raw file](00_preparation.qmd#preparation-data)

## Create a versioned board

We enable versioning so the board retains both writes. We use RDS, an
R format that preserves the column types. The board lives inside our
local workshop outputs.

```{r health-pins-setup, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(
  pins[board_folder, pin_exists, pin_meta, pin_read, pin_versions,
       pin_write],
  utils[read.csv, write.csv]
)

workshop_dir <- file.path("outputs", "health-wellbeing")
data_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "data_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
pin_name <- "health_wellbeing"
versions_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv")
selection_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "analysis-data-version.txt")

write_dataset_version <- function(board, name, data, description, metadata) {
  previous_versions <- character()
  if (pin_exists(board, name)) {
    previous_versions <- pin_versions(board, name)$version
    for (version in previous_versions) {
      if (identical(pin_meta(board, name, version = version)$user, metadata) &&
          identical(pin_read(board, name, version = version), data)) {
        return(version)
      }
    }
  }

  pin_write(
    board,
    data,
    name = name,
    type = "rds",
    title = "HealthWellbeing",
    description = description,
    metadata = metadata
  )
  new_version <- setdiff(pin_versions(board, name)$version, previous_versions)
  stopifnot(length(new_version) == 1L)
  new_version
}
```

## Write and describe two versions

We verify the checksum, load the table from that file, and record its
source and checksum in the pin metadata.

```{r health-pins-write-full, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
source_url <- paste0(
  "https://www.protectlab.org/meta-analysis-in-r/data/",
  "healthwellbeing.rda"
)
raw_file <- file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
raw_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(raw_file))
stopifnot(identical(raw_md5, "0d74964b0b7168379a2b015cb648b326"))

raw_data <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
loaded_names <- load(raw_file, envir = raw_data)
stopifnot(identical(loaded_names, "HealthWellbeing"))
verified_health <- raw_data[["HealthWellbeing"]]
stopifnot(is.data.frame(verified_health), nrow(verified_health) == 29L)

full_version <- write_dataset_version(
  data_board,
  pin_name,
  verified_health,
  description = "All 29 studies in the teaching snapshot.",
  metadata = list(source_url = source_url, raw_md5 = raw_md5, scope = "all")
)
```

For the teaching comparison, we read the exact full pin, then filter
by population. The subset inherits its source and checksum from that
pin. The filter and parent version account for the 11 excluded
studies. The published example uses the full set.

```{r health-pins-write-general, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
full_metadata <- pin_meta(data_board, pin_name, version = full_version)
health_general <- pin_read(data_board, pin_name, version = full_version) |>
  subset(population == "general population")
stopifnot(nrow(health_general) == 18L)

general_version <- write_dataset_version(
  data_board,
  pin_name,
  health_general,
  description = "Only studies labelled general population.",
  metadata = list(
    source_url = full_metadata$user$source_url,
    raw_md5 = full_metadata$user$raw_md5,
    scope = "general",
    filter = "population == 'general population'",
    parent_version = full_version
  )
)

pin_versions(data_board, pin_name)

versions <- data.frame(
  scope = c("all", "general"),
  version = c(full_version, general_version)
)
write.csv(versions, versions_file, row.names = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(selection_file)) {
  writeLines(full_version, selection_file)
}
```

## Try it yourself

Retrieve the full dataset by its recorded identifier and inspect
its source metadata. The selection file starts with the full
version and retains your choice on later runs.

```{r health-pins-read-version, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE, cache.extra = get0("full_version")}
versions <- read.csv(versions_file, colClasses = "character")
full_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "all"]
stopifnot(length(full_version) == 1L)

health_full <- pin_read(data_board, pin_name, version = full_version)
pin_meta(data_board, pin_name, version = full_version)$user
nrow(health_full)
```

## Checkpoint {#pins-checkpoint}

The history includes the full dataset and the subset under distinct
identifiers. Retrieving the full version returns 29 rows. Locate the
identifier of the 18-study subset in
`dataset-versions.csv`. The version identifies a stored object within
this board. If you recreate the board elsewhere, use its new
identifiers and retain the upstream checksum and filter.

Keep the board local and share the source and transformation
instructions when reuse terms are unclear. Next we will make the
selection file a tracked pipeline input.
[Reproducible analytical pipelines](06_targets.qmd)
